name: Mashhadi Persian
notes: Mashhadi Persian (Mašhadī). Iran's second-largest city; capital of Khorasan. Urban Khorasani variety; prestige dialect of northeastern Iran. Conservative vowels (Khorasani base); some imāla in religious/Arabic vocabulary (pilgrimage city: shrine of Imam Reza). /q/ maintained in careful speech. Already-encoded allophones confirmed against the cited sources: ā carries the Khorasani conservative [aː] and a majhul [eː] variant (imāla-adjacent), alongside Tehran's [ɒː] (Windfuhr 2009). The imāla reported in religious/Arabic vocabulary specifically is lexically restricted to loanwords tied to the shrine-city register, not a general phonological rule, so it is documented here but intentionally left unencoded beyond the existing [eː] variant rather than forced.
